47: "And this ... do you ... also ... understand?" "Stop!" whispered I in terror, "or else I will cry out."
45: With an agility, quite unexpected for his age, he flung himself down and stood on his hands, balancing his legs in the air. His white working clothes turned down, his face grew purple and, looking at me fixedly with a strange upturned gaze, he threw at me with difficulty a few broken words,—
43: "The wounded," repeated he, like an echo. "The wounded. Legless and armless, with pierced sides, smashed-in chests and torn-out eyes. You understand it? I am very glad. So I suppose you will understand this also?"
35: Then, in the same solemn and significant manner, he waved his hand towards the row of beds on which the wounded were lying, and repeated,—
33: "And do you understand this?" he asked mysteriously.
31: "Not more than you. Not more than you in any case."
27: I remembered the rain that had frightened us so, and got angry.
25: "They were separated by water being poured over them."
21: "Well, and what of that?" asked I, also in a whisper, full of terror.
19: "You are leaving soon, and I will tell you. Did you ever see a fight in an asylum? No? Well, I saw one. And they fought like sane people. You understand—like sane people." He significantly repeated the last phrase several times.
14: He sat down quite close to me and looking round began whispering rapidly, in a senile way, wagging his sharp, grey little beard.
10: And he was the first to understand me. He hastily nodded his head and repeated,—
5: "A time will come when nobody will be able to go away from here. Yes, neither I nor anybody," and in his old eyes, so close to me, I saw the same fixed, dull, stricken expression. And something terrible, unbearable, resembling the fall of thousands of buildings, darted through my head, and growing cold from terror, I whispered,—
2: And bending over me he whispered through his yellow smoked moustache,—
0: "Yes, there's something wrong," sighed he, and frowned, disappearing in a cloud of tobacco smoke. "I would leave too, if I could."
